steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The choreographic process is the journey from initial idea to a finished dance piece

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: It begins with selecting a stimulus — something that inspires movement creation

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Exploration involves experimenting with movement ideas freely and without judgement

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Selection means choosing the most effective movement material from what was explored

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Name the three main stages of the choreographic process. | Q: Why is exploration an important stage in choreography? | Q: How does the choreographic process support GCSE Dance coursework?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Exploration, selection and refinement — though the process may revisit stages in any order. | Exploration allows the choreographer to experiment freely with movement ideas, generating a wide range of material before deciding what works best. | Documenting each stage provides evidence of creative decision-making, which is assessed in the NEA choreography component.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Use the terms 'exploration, selection, refinement' directly in exam answers — they are key AQA vocabulary Always link your answer to how each stage helps communicate the choreographic intention Mention that the process is cyclical, not linear — examiners look for this understanding Give specific examples of what a choreographer might do at each stage In NEA written tasks, clearly describe each stage you went through with evidence
